transcript:
Speaker A: English ki sabse badi dikkat dimaag mein poora jawab ready hota hai Hindi mein, par English mein bolne baitho to do shabd bhi seedhe nahi nikalte. Mere saath bhi yahi hota tha. Bank gayi thi ek zaroori kaam se. Counter par pahunchi to wahan baithe officer ne English mein tezi se kuch poocha aur ek form meri taraf sarka diya. "Sign here and fill the details." Maine haan, haan bol diya. Par sach to ye tha ki mujhe kuch samajh nahi aaya tha. Peeche logon ki lambi line lagi thi. Sab mujhe hi dekh rahe the. Mujhe laga agar ab poocha to sab sochenge kitni anpadh hai. Ghabrahat mein maine bina padhe galat jagah sign kar diya. Officer chillaya: [The biggest problem with English is that the full answer is ready in your mind in Hindi, but when you sit down to speak in English, not even two words come out straight. The same used to happen to me. I went to the bank for some important work. When I reached the counter, the officer sitting there asked something quickly in English and slid a form towards me. "Sign here and fill the details." I just said yes, yes. But the truth was, I didn't understand anything. There was a long queue of people behind me. Everyone was looking at me. I felt if I asked now, everyone would think I am illiterate. In panic, I signed in the wrong place without reading. The officer yelled:]
Speaker B: "What is this? Can't you read? Maine kaha tha yahan sign mat karna. You are wasting everyone's time." ["What is this? Can't you read? I told you not to sign here. You are wasting everyone's time."]
Speaker A: Usne English mein kuch aur bhi badbad kiya, jo mujhe samajh nahi aaya. Par uske gusse se mera chehra laal ho gaya. Usne zor se aawaz lagayi, "Sharma ji, zara idhar aaiye. Inko Hindi mein samjhaiye. Inko English nahi aati." Manager aaye. Naya form nikala. Mere haath kaanp rahe the. Paseene aa gaye the. Itni sharmindagi mehsoos hui ki mann kiya wahin se bhaag jaun. Ghar aakar roi nahi par mann bahut bhaari tha. Itni si baat thi. Ek form hi to tha. Par main darr gayi kyunki mujhe English nahi aati thi. Main parlor mein kaam karti hun, mehnat se kamati hun, kisi par bojh nahi. Par jahan English aa jaati hai, main chhoti pad jaati hun. Bank ho, hospital ho, har jagah ab English mein baat karni padti hai aur main har jagah atak jaati hun. YouTube dekha par wahi purane grammar rules. Phir mujhe meri dost ne English Seekho app ke baare mein bataya. Maine us raat download kiya. Yahan expert ke chhote-chhote videos the. Bilkul basic se hello se poori conversation tak. Bank, hospital aur daily use hone wali English sikhayi. Ek-ek step, ekdam aasan aur sab Hindi mein samjha ke. Isliye sab dimaag mein baitha. Aur ek AI coach hai Disha. Usse jab time mile bol ke ya likh ke practice kar sakte ho. Poori conversation jaise asli zindagi mein hoti hai. Koi saamne baitha nahi hota isliye galti karne mein sharm nahi aati. Main roz raat ko sone se pehle bas 15 minute deti thi aur dheere-dheere wo haan-haan wali ladki khud poore sentence bolne lagi. Kuch hafte baad phir usi bank gayi. Is baar utna mushkil nahi laga. Is baar khud se poora form bhi bhar liya. Jaate waqt dekha peeche khadi ek aunty counter wale ki English samajh nahi pa rahi thi. Wahi ghabrahat jo us din meri thi. Maine ruk ke unka form bhar diya. Baat samjha di. Unhone kaha, "Beta, tum bahut hoshiyar ho." Chhoti si baat thi par us din khud par garv mehsoos hua. English mushkil nahi, bas kisi ne tumhe theek se sikhaya nahi. Ab expert se seekho apni speed pe, bina sharm ke. English Seekho download karo, ₹1 ka trial lo aur apni jagah khud banao. [He mumbled something else in English which I didn't understand. But my face turned red with his anger. He called out loudly, "Sharma ji, please come here. Explain to her in Hindi. She doesn't know English." The manager came. Took out a new form. My hands were shaking. I was sweating. I felt so embarrassed that I wanted to run away from there. I didn't cry after coming home, but my heart was very heavy. It was such a small thing. It was just a form. But I got scared because I didn't know English. I work in a parlor, earn with hard work, and am not a burden on anyone. But where English comes in, I feel small. Be it a bank or a hospital, now you have to speak in English everywhere and I get stuck everywhere. I watched YouTube but found the same old grammar rules. Then my friend told me about the English Seekho app. I downloaded it that night. There were short videos by experts. From basic hello to full conversations. It taught English used in banks, hospitals, and daily life. Step-by-step, very easy, and explained in Hindi. That's why everything clicked. And there is an AI coach, Disha. You can practice by speaking or writing whenever you find time. Full conversations just like in real life. No one is sitting in front of you, so there is no shame in making mistakes. I used to give just 15 minutes every night before sleeping and gradually that "yes-yes" girl started speaking full sentences herself. A few weeks later, I went to the same bank again. This time it didn't feel that difficult. This time I filled the entire form myself. While leaving, I saw an aunty standing behind who couldn't understand the counter clerk's English. The same panic that was mine that day. I stopped and filled her form. Explained the matter. She said, "Child, you are very smart." It was a small thing, but that day I felt proud of myself. English is not difficult, someone just didn't teach you properly. Now learn from experts at your own speed, without shame. Download English Seekho, take a ₹1 trial, and make your own place.]
